478.frame: APUG 563 f. 179v and f. 181r (crops on the Wuerzburg page, images botschaft_1a.jpg and botschaft_2.jpg)
478.saw: Not the Gregorian repository viewer (EMLO page never loaded; archimede.imss.fi.it/kircher/563/large/ is 403 and the Stanford Luna Insight route is obsolete). I saw two crops of the cryptogram leaves reproduced by Vollrath (Wuerzburg), captioned Ausschnitte aus APUG 563 179v und 181r. 179v: a circle containing a 12x12 grid of the numbers 1-144 in scrambled order (41 80 11 74 12 90 ...), with a 4-line Latin instruction above in Kirchers hand (in quadrato hoc numeros continens ... ). 181r: a circle with a 12x12 grid of Latin syllables (vo tus sint ri prin quan to lu ...), a Latin note above (Jam hic secreta ex praecedenti tabula ...) and a tally of strokes with the number 35. So the cryptogram is a numbered square plus a syllable square, a key-and-message pair, in Latin. No decipherment written on them.
478.note: Page text says the enigma was Kirchers own, sent to the duke, with the dukes receipt dated 29 Sept 1664 answering a letter of 31 Aug; so the cryptogram leaves ff.179-181 look like Kirchers enigma rather than a dukes cryptogram, and the 1 Jun 1664 letter ff.88r-89v was not viewed. Whole leaves not seen, only crops.

568.frame: D 4 Nr. 113/9 image 16 of 18 (p. 17 of the file)
568.saw: Archivportal-D (DDB IIIF) viewer, 18 images of the file (Johann of Hesse-Braubach, 1643); images 9-18 viewed at ~1800 px, cropped to the text half. Image 16 (p.17): German letter of 18 Nov 1643 (Darmstadt/Giessen, signed by the Praesident and Vizekanzler) with two blocks of numeric cipher in the body: first block 6 lines of continuous digit strings of 2-digit groups with no separators (e.g. 39 34 12 30 12 25 14 ... 23 17 26), then clear German words, then a second block of about 5 lines of the same, then clear German again. A small-hand marginal note column sits at the left of the cipher lines, not legible at this size. No decipherment written between lines. Other images: 9 clear German draft with deletions and marginal notes (dated 11 Nov 1643); 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 clear German letters or drafts, no cipher; 17 address leaf with two seals; 18 end label Konv 113.
568.note: Only image 16 carries cipher among images 9-18. Images 1-8 were done in an earlier pass. The two blocks total roughly 11 lines of unseparated digit pairs.
